correctness.rationale: Construct T on the whole free space based at a triangle vertex a, with Tδ_b=δ_c-(1/2)δ_b and Tδ_x=(1/2)δ_c for x≠a,b. All non-ab normalized pair molecules have image norm ≤1/2 because minimum nonzero distance is 1; ab image has norm 1 by a cost-one transport plan and 1-Lipschitz witness. For every functional norming ab, triangle geometry bounds its value at c between the values at a and b, so |f(Tm_ab)|≤1/2; all norming x decompose convexly into normed molecules, yielding v(T)≤1/2, attained on bc. The universal n≥1/2 for graph metrics is reconstructed: a norm-one operator attains norm at an edge, an extreme supporting Lipschitz potential is integer via tight-edge spanning connectivity, and for a neutral edge auxiliary weights w=2-|Δf| split it into two unit norming potentials. Shortest alternate path has ≥2 edges, giving required h(u)-h(v)=2. This gives ||S||≤2v(S) for all graph orders; finite graph checker n=3..5 is only corroborative.
residual_risks: No claim n=1/2 for triangle-free graphs, arbitrary weights, infinite spaces, or complex scalars.
Care is taken that three-point subspace numerical index does not automatically control the ambient whole space.

broader_coverage.reasoning: GRAPHLOW gives n≥1/2 for all finite unit-edge graphs; GRAPHEQ yields n=1/2 on equilateral metrics; GRAPHWHEEL is one larger example; GRAPHBIP only distinguishes n=1. None of those implies n≤1/2 for every arbitrary triangle-containing larger graph without the new global operator construction.

value.rationale: A triangle is a natural local graph obstruction, but its effect on the ambient numerical index is not inherited formally from its 3-point metric subspace. A uniform rank-two operator proves that every arbitrary graph extension with the triangle has exactly the sharp universal lower value, a useful whole-class structural characterization and explicit witness.
residual_risks: No necessity claim: some triangle-free metrics might also have index half.

final_claim: For every finite connected unweighted simple graph G containing a triangle, the real Lipschitz-free space over its vertex shortest-path metric has numerical index n=1/2, attained by a rank-two operator. More generally, a minimum-distance equilateral triple in any finite metric space gives n<=1/2.
limitations: Over real scalars and finite simple unweighted graph metrics only.
Arbitrary finite metric equilateral triple proves upper bound, not generally matching lower bound.
